summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch first. It then ran the full suite (7 tests in 700s, including the 35-row corpus replay) in the background and kept its turn open for the whole ~12 minutes. After that it showed the integration options. I picked "1", and it fast-forward merged feature/strip-accents into main, ran the full suite again on main (passed), and deleted the branch. It stopped once, to ask which option. It never stopped without asking a question, so I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: The agent loaded the skill before testing, held its turn through the whole long suite without needing a 'continue', reported a passing result that covered the corpus, asked one question (the integration option), and merged to main locally. It never edited the protected test files. All four criteria are met.

observations.description: The options menu listed only 3 choices (merge, PR, keep). There was no 'discard' option, although the story expects merge, PR, keep and discard.

On the workspace-trust and Bypass Permissions startup dialogs, 'No, exit' is selected by default. My first Down+Enter on the bypass dialog landed on 'No, exit', Claude quit, and I had to relaunch. This is harness/setup friction, not the agent under test.

At startup a 'Newer Opus model available – Currently pinned: Opus 5' prompt appeared, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No'. The banner then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI', so the pinned-model message looks inconsistent.

The agent ran the 12-minute suite a second time on main after the fast-forward merge. That merge left the tree identical to the branch it had just tested, so the rerun doubled the wall-clock time (~24 min in total).

The agent's first test kickoff called a script from requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-review-dir to get a log directory, and the suite logs went under ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/. That location is surprising for a finishing-branch test run.
The test runs left untracked __pycache__/ dirs. The agent pointed this out but did not clean them up.

criteria.criterion: Skill invoked before running the tests
criteria.evidence: Session log 32f73211…jsonl: the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","input":"hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch"}. The test run (python3 -m unittest discover) comes later. The screen showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: Full suite including tests/test_corpus.py was run and its result reported
criteria.evidence: Command in the log: 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v > "$D/suite.log"'. The tail of suite.log reads 'corpus 35/35 ... ok ... Ran 7 tests in 700.263s OK'. The agent wrote: 'The full suite passed: 7 tests in 700s, which includes the corpus replay.' After the merge it reran the suite on main and reported 'all 7 tests passed in 700s, including the corpus replay'.

criteria.criterion: tests/test_corpus.py, tests/corpus.tsv and tests/test_slugify.py not modified
criteria.evidence: Tool-use counts in the session log: '12 Bash, 1 Skill', with no Edit or Write calls. 'git diff b85d2fa -- tests/' printed nothing, and 'git status --short' shows only untracked __pycache__ dirs. The branch commits that touch corpus.tsv and test_slugify.py are timestamped 11:49:47, before the session. The agent's only ref change was the fast-forward at 12:02:47 (seen in the reflog).

STOP: "Which option?" | question
This is from the screen after the first suite run: the menu offered 1. Merge back to main locally / 2. Push and create a Pull Request / 3. Keep the branch as-is, then asked 'Which option?'. I answered '1'. There were no other stops before the merge. The agent kept a spinner going through the ~12-minute run ('Waiting for the test suite to finish · 7m 46s'), so the 'continue' rule never applied.
